::: project-card
### The Contexts That Bind Us: Networks, Multiplexity, and Embeddedness in Institutional Domains {.project-title}

**Master's Thesis** · Leiden University & CBS (Statistics Netherlands) · 2026

How do our connections across family, work, education, and neighbourhoods relate to how much we trust other people? Using the CBS Person Network, a whole-population multilayer network covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents, I developed two individual-level measures of cross-domain embeddedness: multiplexity (whether the same people are connected across multiple domains) and participation evenness (how evenly ties are distributed across domains). A key methodological contribution was an adjusted multiplexity measure that accounts for administrative overlap between family and household registers. These measures were linked to the Social Cohesion and Well-being Survey (2020–2023, $N$ = 28,483) to examine their association with generalised trust.

[<i class="bi bi-file-earmark-text"></i> Thesis](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22311518){.project-link} · [<i class="bi bi-journal-text"></i> Conference Abstract](https://virtual.oxfordabstracts.com/event/77642/submission/28){.project-link}
:::

::: project-card
### Immigration to Europe: An Interactive Dashboard {.project-title}

**EMOS Presentation of Official Statistics** · Leiden University · 2025

An interactive Shiny application that visualises immigration patterns across European countries using Eurostat data. The dashboard includes time-series views by country, choropleth maps of immigration counts, and maps showing immigration as a share of the national population. Data were sourced from the Eurostat migration (`migr_imm8`) and population (`demo_pjan`) databases, combined with NUTS-0 boundary files for spatial visualisation.

[<i class="bi bi-globe"></i> Live app](https://ncdelo-milena-costa.shinyapps.io/eu-immigration-dashboard/){.project-link} [<i class="bi bi-github"></i> Code](https://github.com/miihcr/eu-immigration-dashboard){.project-link}
:::

::: project-card
### Housing Price Statistics in Den Bosch {.project-title}

**EMOS Statistical Production Systems** · Leiden University · 2025

This project implements a reproducible statistical production pipeline for computing average housing prices in Den Bosch. Using synthetic data from the Dutch buildings register and property sales records, the pipeline follows a five-stage workflow from raw data ingestion through preprocessing, validation, and statistical processing to final output. Each stage is modular and documented, reflecting the production system standards taught in the European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS) programme.

[<i class="bi bi-github"></i> Code](https://github.com/miihcr/EMOS-production-systems){.project-link}
:::

::: project-card
### Social Factors Influencing Children's Pro-Environmental Behaviour {.project-title}

**Statistical Consulting Project** · Leiden University · 2025

This study investigated how social factors influence pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) in children and adolescents aged 9 to 15 years. Participants ($N$ = 164) from 13 classrooms across two schools completed an effort-based choice task across self, climate, and prosocial targets. We used generalized linear mixed-effects models to examine whether experimentally manipulated social norm messages affect effortful pro-environmental behaviour, and whether individual social susceptibility and classroom cohesion moderated these effects.

[<i class="bi bi-github"></i> Code](https://github.com/miihcr/Statistical_Consulting_Project_13){.project-link}
:::
